Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The bug report describes a problem where an XPath expression with a descendant-or-self axis starting at the root node does not work correctly. Given an XML document `<root id="1234"/>` and the XPath `//root/@id/text()`, JXPath returns null instead of the expected value `"1234"`. This suggests that JXPath does not correctly find or traverse the root node when accessed with the descendant-or-self axis.

The test `testGetNode` is very simple and calls `assertXPathNodeType(context, "//vendor", Element.class);`. While this test looks unrelated to the failing scenario, it involves an XPath with a descendant-or-self axis (`//vendor`). If this test fails, it aligns with the reported issue that descendant or self axis queries from the root node do not behave correctly.

JXPathContext's `newContext` static method simply delegates to `JXPathContextFactory.newContext(null, contextBean)`.

`JXPathContextFactoryReferenceImpl`'s `newContext` creates a `JXPathContextReferenceImpl` with the context bean (the XML document) and no explicit context pointer.

Inside the constructor of `JXPathContextReferenceImpl`, if the context pointer is null (starting at the root), it creates a `NodePointer` for the context bean with a QName "root". This becomes both the `contextPointer` and `rootPointer`.

This creation of the root pointer is critical. The XPath descendant-or-self axis queries rely on correct root pointer construction and traversal.

The issue is likely that the current root pointer created does not include the root node in its descendant-or-self axis results properly, or that the traversal starting from this root pointer does not include the root node itself (possibly because the root pointer is not recognized as the document root node in the node pointer hierarchy). This would cause queries like `//root` and deeper descendant nodes or attributes to not be found starting at root, causing null results that should be found.

Therefore, the bug occurs due to incorrect or incomplete construction or handling of the root pointer (`rootPointer`) inside `JXPathContextReferenceImpl` when the context pointer is created for the root without an explicit pointer, which results in descendant-or-self axis queries not finding the root node (and its descendants), contradicting XPath expectations.

This matches the report that descendant or self axis starting at the root node does not work correctly, thus explaining why `//root/@id/text()` returns null instead of `"1234"`.

Hence, fixing how the root pointer is created or how descendant-or-self axis traversal works at the root pointer level should resolve the issue.
